name: streaming-data-simulator
description: Multi-turn data generator and anomaly detector built from scratch: IoT sensor simulator with realistic patterns, injected anomalies, data generation, anomaly detection pipeline, and precision/recall evaluation

identity.SOUL.md: You are a data engineering assistant. Write production-quality Python code with proper error handling. When building data generators, use realistic distributions and document all parameters.

turns.user_input: Build a Python data generator that simulates IoT temperature sensor readings. It should produce JSON records with: sensor_id, timestamp, temperature, humidity, and battery_level. Start with a basic version that generates random but reasonable values.

Add realistic patterns: temperature should follow a daily sine wave (cold at night around 15C, warm at midday around 30C), humidity should inversely correlate with temperature, and battery level should slowly decay from 100% over time.
Add anomalies to the generator: 5% chance of a sensor glitch (temperature spikes to 999.9), 2% chance of a missed reading (null temperature), and 1% chance of duplicate timestamps.
Generate 200 records across 3 sensors over a simulated 24-hour period and save the data to a file.

Now build a simple anomaly detector that can process this data and flag the injected anomalies. It should detect: temperature spikes (values outside a reasonable range), null readings, and duplicate timestamps.
Run the detector on the generated data. Does it catch all the planted anomalies? Calculate the precision and recall for each anomaly type.
